Subject: Shipping plan to meet all demand at the lowest total transportation cost
Date: [Insert date]
From: Supply Chain Director
To: Operations, Transportation, Finance

Situation
We operate a multi-node network with several warehouses, factories, and distribution centers supplying a broad set of stores and customer locations. Transportation rates vary by origin–destination lane, and inventory is unevenly distributed across sources. To protect margins and service, we need a clear, lane-by-lane plan that uses the most economical routes while ensuring every location gets what it needs. All moves must be in whole units (no partial loads).

Problem
Each source has limited available inventory and handling capacity. Each destination has a defined requirement that must be covered within the planning horizon. Lane costs differ across the network, so sending the same product from different sources can lead to very different landed costs. The challenge is to determine how much to ship from each source to each destination—strictly in whole-unit quantities—so that:
- No source ships more than it has available.
- Every destination receives its full requirement.
- The total transportation spend is kept as low as possible, favoring lower-cost lanes without creating shortages or over-allocations.

Approach and next steps
- Validate data: Confirm available inventory at each source and required quantities at each destination; confirm the latest lane rates and accessorials.
- Build the plan: Allocate shipments across lanes in whole units, prioritizing lower-cost routes where supply is available and ensuring destination needs are fully covered.
- Check feasibility: Confirm operational practicality (loading, carrier capacity, transit times) and provide alternates if primary low-cost lanes are saturated.
- Review and approval: Deliver a recommended shipping schedule showing lane-by-lane quantities in whole units and the expected total freight spend for sign-off.
- Execution and monitoring: Hand off to Transportation for tendering and track performance; adjust if supply positions or rates change.

The attached data will drive the plan. Once validated, we will produce a recommended routing that meets all demand without exceeding any source’s inventory and that lowers overall costs versus ad hoc allocation. This will help avoid stockouts, stabilize service levels, and capture near-term savings across the network.
